disposition_reason: Table 3 prints per-wine arsenic, cadmium, mercury, lead, nickel and chromium concentrations for 13 Romanian wines.

study.design: method validation with application to retail wines
study.origin: Romanian vineyards (Cotnari, Recas, Prahova, Jidvei, Murfatlar)
study.method: ICP-Q-MS (PerkinElmer ELAN DRC-e) after 10-20x dilution with ultrapure water
study.qa: synthetic 1% alcohol sample spiked at 2 µg/L: bias 0.8-17%; repeatability SD 0.09-0.5 µg/L; no CRM

unresolved: Lead and nickel values are identical in three rows (Tamâioasa romaneasca 2005, Rosu Dulce, Pinot Noir 2007), suggesting a column transcription error.
Lead expanded uncertainty at 2 µg/L is 2.897 µg/L (Table 2), larger than the value itself, so low lead results are poorly determined.
Mercury values of 81.14, 200 and 53.94 µg/L in three white wines are far above typical wine levels; not resolvable from the paper.
Only wine was measured; no slightly alcoholic beverage or spirit samples.
Wine year labels are vintages, not collection dates.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: OIV maximum levels for metals in wine referenced; Pb, Cd and As were below them
